approval.prompt: Stylized low-poly 3D game asset with a clean, readable silhouette and slightly exaggerated proportions. findings.observation: The planted feet slide at p90 1.10 m/s (max 1.13) over the 16 contact frames at the start of the clip (0 to about 0.25 s), and both feet shuffle at about 0.9 m/s before they lift. The tolerances report this only for deaths, because the feet kick out while the body collapses onto pinned Hips, so it is not asserted. The largest foot speeds (3.2 to 3.6 m/s around 0.8 to 0.9 s) come after the feet leave the ground, as the legs swing up during the fall.
findings.evidence: assets/manifests/barrow_levy/judge/motion-death-1/03_plots.png (ground-relative speed and heights panels); metrics foot_slide_p90_mps, foot_slide_max_mps, contact_frames

findings.observation: Because the Hips are pinned, the fall pivots around the origin: the legs swing forward and up (about 0.44 m foot height at 1.1 to 1.3 s) and the torso lands behind the origin. In the side onion skin, parts of the final red pose seem to reach slightly below the floor line. The final Hips height stays at about 0.07 m, so this is most likely projection or depth in the view, not real ground penetration. The evidence doesn't settle it, and it would only be visible up close.

judgments.summary: The Front-file death clip keeps the Hips pinned at the origin and collapses into a clean supine pose with no broken joints or stretch; all three assertions pass, and the only issue is a reported-only foot slide the tolerances already accept for deaths.
The Front-file run clip stays in place, its planted feet hold, and the frame strip shows no broken poses; all four assertions pass.

findings.observation: Worst single-frame planted-foot speed is 0.769 m/s, only at lift-off and touch-down; mid-stance near 0 and p90 0.172 m/s. Not visible at gameplay distance.
Hips sway about 0.06 m side to side, normal walk weight shift; ends at 0.00 m.

judgments.summary: The Back-file run clip (Walk_Loop) stays in place, its planted feet hold, and it shows no broken poses or stretching; all four assertions pass.
